findings.title: Login-cache invalidation on update compares org-aware wrapped 'original' against raw 'updated' model and can skip a needed invalidation
findings.body: update() obtains the pre-update state via getById() (line 91), which returns the organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() additionally returns false when the linked organization is disabled. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate then evaluates getLoginPredicate() on this wrapped 'original' but on the raw 'updated' model. The cached getForLogin ID sets, however, are computed from the raw store filters (raw enabled/linkOnly/hideOnLogin/BROKER_PUBLIC), so the wrapper's org-dependent isEnabled() makes the comparison inconsistent: if the linked organization is currently disabled, getLoginPredicate().test(original) is false even though the IDP's ID is still present in the cached login sets. If the same update then removes the IDP from the login set (e.g. sets hideOnLogin=true, disables it, or clears BROKER_PUBLIC), test(updated) is also false, the early return at line 405 fires, and the login caches are not invalidated. The stale ID remains cached; once the organization is re-enabled (organization updates do not invalidate these caches), the now hidden/disabled/non-public IDP reappears on the login page, because OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-checks isEnabled() and does not re-check hideOnLogin/linkOnly/BROKER_PUBLIC. The original state used for the comparison should be the raw model (e.g. obtained from idpDelegate.getById, or the predicate should not rely on the wrapped isEnabled()).

findings.title: Cleanup registers removal of literal alias "alias" instead of the created identity providers
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, cleanup after creating each identity provider is registered as getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) (lines 381 and 425; the same copy-paste mistake already exists in testCacheIDPByOrg at line 303). The literal string "alias" is used instead of the actual provider alias ("idp-alias-" + i), so the roughly 20 identity providers created by the test are never removed and leak into the shared test realm, where they can pollute subsequent tests that enumerate or display identity providers. Additionally, the cleanup DELETE for the non-existent alias "alias" will return 404, which may surface as a cleanup failure. The real alias of each created IDP should be passed to get(...).
